answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond and lists work in a subcontract ledger. Each link bears an onyx seal binding subcontractor key, work, and payer, so an auditor can recompute the chain. A hollow shell passing work onward earns no own-work share, and a chain deeper than the zenith cap of two links is frozen, its bond burned. The k-th fake still needs 80 bond plus 40 credits of real work, so 1,000 fakes cost 120,000; an honest agent pays 120 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch. A rented-shell ring fails because its seals show zero own work and both bonds burn.
